strengths.description:
The contribution has a specific and appropriately limited identity

The paper identifies its contribution as connecting conditional word-7 identities, paired finalization effects, and spectral reconstruction on fresh keys. It distinguishes that contribution from familiar weak low-round diffusion and from improvements in attack complexity. This makes the proposed addition assessable without requiring the manuscript to become a new attack paper. The abstract and conclusion maintain the same diagnostic scope.

strengths.description:
The central local result is developed within the article

The conditional map, rank formula, singleton-response identity, and proof are present in the main text. The subsequent explanation distinguishes conditional behavior of one word from joint affinity or a full-cipher rank statement. From an editorial perspective, this is useful self-contained exposition: readers can inspect the claimed local contribution without consulting a supplementary manuscript.

strengths.description:
The cohort overview supports navigation across experiments

The overview makes the changes in output length, pooling, rounds, and cohort purpose visible before the detailed measurements. This is particularly valuable in a paper containing several related experimental stages.

strengths.description:
The figures expose the main observable distinctions

The rendered panels and captions are legible and organize the results around position, rotation, spectral prediction, and the round transition. Figure 2 separates the unfinalized derivative response from the fundamental-power contrast under modular finalization. Figure 1 distinguishes a four-position profile from an output-word contrast. These distinctions support the paper's emphasis on what each measurement actually summarizes.

weaknesses.description:
The six-setting model comparison is overly compressed

The paper reports spectrum-error ranges across resolutions and gives selected numerical predictions at 128 bits. This makes the stated tradeoff between spectrum reconstruction and entropy-gap accuracy harder to inspect for the other two widths. Figure 2 also displays only the 128-bit spectra. Replace part of the numerical paragraph with a compact comparison indexed by cipher and width, or use clearly labelled triples, showing the existing observed/predicted gaps and spectrum errors. The purpose is to make the reported six-setting comparison visible in the article; no additional simulation or hypothesis test is needed. This affects clarity rather than the stated contribution.

strengths.description:
The independent unit matches the design and resampling

Each principal analysis retains 80 key pairs as independent replicates and keeps masks, bases, blocks, and interventions within those pairs. The paper distinguishes fresh-key cohorts from repeated analysis of existing trajectories and explicitly identifies reuse of the resolution cohort for model training. The inspected analysis code resamples whole rows of key-level endpoints, preserving the relevant within-key dependencies. This avoids treating the many masks, blocks, deterministic checkpoints, or simulated pseudo-keys as additional experimental key replicates.

strengths.description:
The measurement definitions support interpretable comparisons

The order of power averaging, normalization, and entropy calculation is explicit, as are changes in pooling between alignment and complete scans. The DC/AC decomposition explains why entropy is not monotonic in mean diffusion strength. Defining the fundamental fraction separately from the sum of block harmonics also makes the round-transition endpoint interpretable. The rotation control preserves the HW multiset and DC share, providing a useful intervention on the measurement while leaving the cipher unchanged.

evidence_anchor.locator: Equations labeled eq:entropy, eq:identity, and eq:gapfundamental in Direct and Spectral Measurements.

strengths.description:
The algebra and transition experiment support appropriately local conclusions

The proof identifies disjoint active column supports and explains both the rank formula and the bounded mean singleton response. Its assumptions concern a fixed remaining state and one output-word map; the prose explicitly prevents extrapolation to joint affinity or full-cipher rank. The third-round experiment then checks nonzero within-word second derivatives of the unfinalized map, while the persistent block-scale observable comes from standard output. These are distinct measurements, and the conclusion preserves that distinction. As a stored-data consistency check, the 80 Salsa20 round-three, unfinalized key-level rows average to the reported raw response at the displayed precision; this does not turn 10,240 repeated evaluations into 10,240 independent keys.

strengths.description:
The predictive comparison uses the actual nonlinear estimator and reports counterexamples to uniform improvement

The model implementation samples the stated M0 marginals and M1 key/base-conditional distributions, then applies the same finite-sample estimator used for evaluation. It does not replace expected entropy by the entropy of expected power. The inspected summaries agree with the manuscript's six-cell sign agreement, smaller M1 mean-spectrum errors, and the opposing entropy-gap rankings for ChaCha20 and Salsa20. Separate Monte Carlo errors and the explicit conditioning of evaluation intervals on the fixed fit prevent simulated sample size from being presented as training-cohort precision. The manuscript also acknowledges that mean spectra can conceal mask-level errors and does not present these intervals as model-rejection tests.

strengths.description:
The strength of the conclusions tracks the strength of the evidence

The direct benchmark is identified as following the original spectral findings, rather than as a prospective power comparison. Pointwise intervals that include zero are not treated as equivalence, and small higher-round departures are not converted into a security conclusion. The feed-forward and conditional-affinity results are likewise restricted to the tested constructions and observables. These limitations leave a coherent, narrower mechanistic contribution.

weaknesses.description:
The main endpoint table should carry the calibration qualification

The Methods correctly state that zero mean does not imply sign-invariance and that Holm adjustment is conditional on valid endpoint calibration. The central table labels its column simply as Holm p and mentions the simulation floor, but omits the assumption-dependent interpretation. A reader using the table alone could therefore mistake these values for established distribution-free tests of the stated mean-zero null. Relabel the column as a Holm-adjusted sign-flip calibration and add a short caption qualification referring to the sign-invariance assumption. This is a presentation repair: the large reported effects, whole-key intervals, deterministic identities, and explicit Methods caveat do not warrant a major methodological penalty. Stronger unconditional testing claims would require their own justification or analysis, but the present article need not make those claims.

strengths.description:
The conditional Salsa20 word map and its rank are correctly derived

The two word-7 updates yield a map of the form W2[7] = u XOR C with C independent of the second nonce word when the remaining state is fixed. The displayed expression for C follows the column and row update order. For the finalized map, each active input bit produces the carry interval beginning one position above that bit and ending at the next zero of C, or at the word boundary. Those intervals are disjoint. This supports both the affine representation over F2 and the count of independent columns, including the inactive most significant input bit. Their union also gives the stated mean singleton HW bound and the trailing-ones formula. The manuscript properly limits the rank to this conditional output-word map and identifies its contrasting constants as algebraic examples. The inspected corollary code and saved summary are consistent with this derivation; the reported deterministic checks are supporting records rather than a substitute for the proof.

evidence_anchor.locator: Results, Round Function: Recurring Structure and Conditional Rank, eq:compactfC and eq:affinecorollary

strengths.description:
The dependency and finalization statements preserve the relevant distinctions

The stated Salsa20 missing paths agree with the two-round schedule, and adding the initial state does not reintroduce the missing nonce dependencies in the listed output words. The none/xor second-derivative equality follows directly from the affine dependence of the initial state on the nonce. For word 7, conditional affinity in the second nonce word does not prevent a mixed derivative when the first nonce word changes C; the displayed difference of L_b columns correctly captures that distinction. The saved interaction summary matches the reported raw response and reference-adjusted interaction. The manuscript also correctly avoids interpreting ChaCha's cyclic state symmetry as invariance of the distribution of valid initialized states.

strengths.description:
The third-round observation has the correct logical scope

The inspected round evaluator places the before/after checkpoints around the c update of quarter round (15,3,7,11), which is the sole write to word 7 in that round. The saved checkpoint summaries agree with the reported zero-to-nonzero transition for the two selected within-word pairs. A nonzero second derivative is sufficient to refute affinity for the corresponding fixed context. The text explicitly confines that conclusion to the unfinalized map and does not extrapolate it to all contexts, the finalized map, or the earliest nonlinear operation elsewhere. Comparing that local witness with a remaining standard-output spectral signal is therefore a defensible comparison of two different observables.

strengths.description:
Spectral entropy is interpreted as a measurement of difference trajectories

The definitions distinguish entropy of the pooled power spectrum from entropy of keystream bits. The DC/AC decomposition and the Parseval expression explain why a higher full-spectrum entropy need not imply stronger diffusion. Frequency B = W/512 identifies the 512-bit fundamental under the stated sampling convention, and the manuscript distinguishes that fraction from a sum over harmonics. It also treats segment aggregation as a change of observable. These qualifications make the reported resolution-dependent entropy gaps and the weaker mean response with higher entropy scientifically interpretable without assigning an unjustified security ordering.

strengths.description:
The prediction claims match the empirical models and reported errors

The independent-residual expected-power formula is appropriate for the stated conditional models, and the code implements the distinct pooling in M0 and conditioning in M1. The manuscript correctly separates normalized expected power from the expected finite-sample entropy and uses simulated outputs for the latter comparison. The inspected compact summary supports the reported 128-bit fundamental contrasts, Salsa20 gap, and MCSE. Crucially, the text reports the settings where M1 does not improve the entropy gap and acknowledges that averaged spectra can hide mask-level discrepancies. Thus the conclusion concerns reconstruction of selected summaries, without claiming a complete generative model of the cipher responses.

strengths.description:
Cryptographic implications remain proportionate to the evidence

The study distinguishes fixed-key nonce-response diagnostics from a key-recovery attack and does not infer full-round security or insecurity from these observables. It acknowledges that direct diagnostics detect the same large reduced-round departures and that no calibrated detector-power advantage was established. Its express limitation of novelty concerning weak two-round diffusion and higher-order differences is appropriate to the claims actually advanced. These boundaries permit the algebraic and experimental results to stand as diagnostic findings without an unsupported claim of cryptanalytic improvement.

strengths.description:
The entropy observable and its interpretation are clearly separated

The paper specifies that the signal consists of segmentwise Hamming weights of nonce-induced output differences. Its decomposition of full-spectrum entropy into DC share and normalized AC entropy gives a useful explanation of why a larger reported entropy need not mean a stronger diffusion response. Section 4.4 makes the implication concrete through the Salsa20 example with fewer changed bits but higher entropy. This is a substantive bridge between the language of entropy in signal analysis and the meaning of diffusion in cryptography.

strengths.description:
The alignment intervention has an interpretable and bounded purpose

Preserving the Hamming-weight multiset, mean, variance, and DC share while rotating samples within blocks makes the measurement intervention understandable without knowledge of the detailed cipher schedule. Figure 1 connects the positional profile to the loss of AC contrast under rotation. The text also prevents readers from treating the reported 96% and 94% reductions as security margins. The direct benchmark and discussion explicitly limit the contribution to explaining an already detectable response rather than asserting a detector-power advantage.

strengths.description:
Local algebraic conclusions retain their proper scope

The discussion distinguishes the conditional map of one output word from a joint map over the full state, and identifies the constants used to compare ranks as illustrations rather than observed cipher states. Section 4.3 similarly separates nonzero derivative witnesses for the unfinalized word from block-scale structure in finalized output. These qualifications help readers understand why a local loss of affinity and a persistent spectral feature can coexist, and why neither supplies a secure-round threshold.

strengths.description:
The model comparison exposes the limits of spectral reconstruction

The observed and predicted spectra provide a direct visual connection between positional modeling and frequency-domain structure. The caption identifies conjugate-bin folding, DC omission, Nyquist treatment, and the absence of reference subtraction. The methods distinguish entropy of expected power from expected finite-sample entropy, while the results acknowledge that M1's better mean spectra do not make it better for every entropy gap. Reporting the Monte Carlo error separately from the residual prediction error further helps readers distinguish simulation precision from model adequacy.

strengths.description:
The units of evidence are made accessible across disciplines

The cohort table separates output length, pooling, and round count, and identifies the training cohort's reuse. The accompanying explanations distinguish fresh keys from independent investigators, preserve the whole key as the resampling unit, and state that deterministic checkpoints and simulations do not enlarge the empirical cohorts. These details make the numerical evidence easier to interpret for readers accustomed to different meanings of replication.

weaknesses.description:
Add a plain-language interpretation of conditional affinity and rank

The proof specifies the affine map and its independent columns, but the prose moves directly from XOR-affinity to finite-field rank without explaining what either quantity means operationally. Because the rank-versus-mean comparison is a central contribution, a signal-processing or statistics reader should not have to infer that connection solely from the proof. Add two brief sentences explaining that, with the other inputs fixed, XOR-affinity means a constant output offset plus a linear combination over binary arithmetic, and that rank counts independent output-change directions generated by the input bits. Then state explicitly that the average number of changed bits measures a different property, which is why the equal-mean example can have different ranks. The existing equations, proof, and restrictions can remain; this is an explanatory repair rather than a request to expand the study.

strengths.description: The most consequential possible counterexample would be a carry interaction that invalidates the claimed conditional affinity. The proof addresses this: each active input bit induces an interval ending at the next zero of the fixed constant, and successive active intervals are disjoint. Their independence supports the rank formula, while the union of their supports supports the singleton-HW formula. The manuscript also prevents an invalid extrapolation from this conditional map to joint affinity or full-cipher rank. The constants illustrating equal means with different ranks are explicitly presented as algebraic examples, so their use does not require demonstrating their occurrence among sampled cipher states.

strengths.competence_basis: direct algebraic inspection of the stated conditional map.

strengths.description: The finalization argument distinguishes an existing asymmetry from an added interaction. The positive working-output gap and the positive add-minus-none increment are different endpoints, and the manuscript does not infer that modular addition created the whole gap. Reusing the working state makes the intervention interpretable within these constructions. The mixed word-7 derivative is likewise distinguished from restoration of a reference-sized response, so a small nonzero interaction is not presented as adequate diffusion.

strengths.description: The third-round result avoids another potentially invalid implication. A nonzero second derivative disproves affinity for the sampled unfinalized maps, but does not by itself establish the corresponding property after modular finalization or identify the first nonlinear operation in the entire state. Those restrictions appear in the manuscript itself. The simultaneous spectral observation is expressly taken from standard output; the conclusion reports coexistence of these two observations rather than claiming they are the same observable.

strengths.description: The prediction claims also survive comparison with the supplied summaries. M1 has smaller mean-spectrum distances and smaller absolute fundamental-fraction errors in all six settings. M0 nevertheless has smaller absolute entropy-gap errors in all three ChaCha20 settings, as the manuscript states. Consequently, the argument does not silently turn improvement of a mean spectrum into improvement of every nonlinear summary. The reported Salsa20 128-bit residual also exceeds its simulation MCSE, and is disclosed rather than absorbed into a claim of exact reconstruction. These checks corroborate the reported comparisons; they do not independently validate the frozen fits or the complete data pipeline.
